title: 2nd Stopping Place 2nd Truth The Absoluteness Of Dominical Acts 1st Example From Sura Al Nahl

questions.question: Which living thing is used as the main example in this passage?
questions.answer: The bee.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah taught the bee to do?
questions.answer: He taught it to make its home in the mountains.

questions.question: Why is the bee called a wonder of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Because even though it is tiny, it is made with amazing abilities and a special job.

questions.question: What are three special things mentioned about the bee’s body?
questions.answer: It has a tiny head with a plan for its work, a small stomach that prepares sweet food, and a sting with poison that does not harm itself.

questions.question: What do these details about the bee show about how it was made?
questions.answer: They show great wisdom, care, balance, and purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can nature or accident not be the maker of the bee’s abilities?
questions.answer: Because such careful and balanced work cannot come from something blind, careless, or without knowledge.

questions.question: How are bees found across the earth in a way that supports the main message?
questions.answer: They are found in many places but are made in the same wise and orderly way.

questions.question: What main belief does the example of the bees prove?
questions.answer: It proves Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The amazing design and order in bees clearly show that one wise Creator made them.

questions.question: What Qur’an example is brought at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The example of Allah inspiring the bee.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the bee’s task?
questions.answer: It has an important duty to carry out.

questions.question: What is placed in the bee’s head?
questions.answer: A full plan for doing its work.

questions.question: What happens in the bee’s stomach?
questions.answer: Delicious food is prepared there.

questions.question: What is unusual about the bee’s sting?
questions.answer: It contains poison that can harm other living things but does not injure the bee itself.

questions.question: What kind of qualities are needed to make a creature like this?
questions.answer: Knowledge, care, wisdom, and clear purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage say cannot take part in making the bee?
questions.answer: Unconscious nature and random accident cannot take part.

questions.question: Why does seeing the same kind of bee all over the world strengthen the proof?
questions.answer: Because it shows one Maker is creating them all with the same wisdom and order.

questions.question: What conclusion should a reader make from the bee example?
questions.answer: Allah alone is the Creator, and this is clear from how bees are made.

questions.question: What animal does the passage focus on to teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It focuses on the bee.

questions.question: Where is the bee told to make its dwelling?
questions.answer: In the mountains.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the bee in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It describes the bee as an amazing sign of Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why is the bee’s small size important in this argument?
questions.answer: Because such great skill and planning are placed in a very tiny creature.

questions.question: What does the bee’s inner design teach us about its Creator?
questions.answer: It teaches that its Creator has perfect knowledge and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage use the making of honey-like food as evidence?
questions.answer: It shows that the bee is equipped in a precise and beneficial way that could not happen by accident.

questions.question: What idea is shown by the fact that the sting hurts others but not the bee itself?
questions.answer: It shows careful design and control in how the bee was made.

questions.question: What does the repeated pattern of bees around the world tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us that one Lord made them all in the same balanced way.

questions.question: If something is made with wisdom, order, and purpose, what does the passage say about random causes?
questions.answer: It says random causes cannot be responsible for it.

questions.question: What instruction from Allah to the bee is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The bee was guided to find a place to live in the mountains.

questions.question: Why is a whole surah named after the bee, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because the bee is a remarkable example of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What is special about the program placed in the bee’s head?
questions.answer: It directs the bee in doing its important work.

questions.question: What benefit is placed in the bee’s stomach?
questions.answer: Sweet food is produced there.

questions.question: What dangerous thing is placed in the bee’s sting?
questions.answer: A poison that can kill living creatures.

questions.question: Why is it important that the poison does not hurt the bee itself?
questions.answer: It shows the bee was made with exact care and wise planning.

questions.question: Which is the better explanation for the bee’s design in this passage: blind nature or Allah’s wisdom?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage connect many bees on earth to belief in Allah?
questions.answer: Their matching design and order everywhere point to one Creator.

questions.question: What proof is called clear and easy to see in this passage?
questions.answer: The way bees are made and spread across the world is clear proof of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Which creature in the passage is described almost like a machine for making sweetness?
questions.answer: The bee.

questions.question: What shows that the bee has guidance for its job from the beginning?
questions.answer: A complete plan for its work is placed in its tiny head.

questions.question: What does the passage say is made ready inside the bee for people to think about?
questions.answer: Delicious nourishment is prepared inside it.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the bee’s poison with its own safety?
questions.answer: The poison can harm others, but the bee itself stays unharmed.

questions.question: What do all these features together show about the bee’s creation?
questions.answer: They show it was created with perfect order, balance, and wisdom.

questions.question: Why would it be wrong, based on the passage, to say the bee came to be through accident?
questions.answer: Because accident cannot produce such careful, meaningful design.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the same pattern appears in countless bees over the earth?
questions.answer: Bees everywhere are made with the same wise design and purpose.

questions.question: What belief should grow stronger when someone studies the bee in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the best summary of this passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: The bee’s amazing design and the same design in bees worldwide clearly show one wise Creator.

questions.question: What small creature is presented as a strong sign of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: The bee.

questions.question: What place is mentioned as a home for the bee?
questions.answer: The mountains.

questions.question: What part of the bee contains a plan for its work?
questions.answer: Its tiny head.

questions.question: What part of the bee prepares sweet food?
questions.answer: Its small stomach.

questions.question: What part of the bee carries something harmful to other creatures?
questions.answer: Its sting.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying the bee is not harmed by its own sting?
questions.answer: It teaches that the bee was designed with great precision and care.

questions.question: Which qualities of creation are repeated in the passage to explain the bee?
questions.answer: Wisdom, care, balance, and purpose.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject blind nature as the cause of the bee’s design?
questions.answer: Because blind nature cannot make something so orderly and exact.

questions.question: How do countless bees across the world become evidence for tawhid?
questions.answer: Their shared design in every place points to one Allah who made them all.
